explanation: Track the previous two prefix counts as BigInt values. A nonzero final digit extends the previous prefix; a final pair from 10 through 26 extends the prefix before it. Convert the final guaranteed 32-bit result to Number.
timeComplexity: O(n) arithmetic operations for n digits; big-integer costs depend on intermediate count width. Each digit performs a constant number of count operations; counts have at most O(n) bits, so O(n squared) bit time is a safe upper bound.
spaceComplexity: Two arbitrary-precision integer counts, using O(n) bits in the worst case. Only a constant number of arbitrary-precision counts coexist, each with O(n) bits.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 JavaScript algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: A decoding of each prefix ends with either a valid nonzero single digit or a valid pair from 10 through 26. Removing that final token gives a decoding of the preceding one- or two-shorter prefix. Those cases are disjoint and exhaustive, so adding their counts yields exactly all decodings. Arbitrary-precision intermediate counts prevent overflow before the final int result.
walkthrough: For "1213", the valid tokenizations are 1|2|1|3,12|1|3,1|21|3,1|2|13 and 12|13. There are five, so return 5.
edgeCases: A leading zero has no decoding.
Zero can occur only within a valid pair such as 10 or 20.
Each digit must belong to exactly one token.
